<subject>Re: Results of the Insolvency Hearing for Eastwick's Issues With Commercial Lending</subject>
<body>
You should have the email below in your inbox talking about the clients on the Corporate Lending system. Reply to the email below once you find out if you are able to process the client's loans without maintaining a minimum balance.
</body>
<quoted>
-----Original Message-----
From: 	Owen, Julia  
Sent:	Tuesday, April 29, 2025 4:09 PM
To:	Hamilton, Derek; Hutchinson, Ross; Johnston, Laura; Marian Hussain, Debra
Cc:	Sophie Jr., Ed; Mann, Gregory; m796@maroragroup.com'; s692@soldynlabs.com'; Barker, Mathew; Amy, Joshua; Garza, Kathleen; m789@trinorco.com'; j244@trinorco.com'; Holmes, Sean A.
Subject:	Results of the Insolvency Hearing for Eastwick's Issues With Commercial Lending

Here is a quick update on how Eastwick Financial, Eastwick, insolvency hearing went last week for the Commercial Lending issues:

Eastwick agreed to withdraw the portion of their motion that was associated with Commercial Lending. The bank admitted that Commercial Lending has been utilising their credit facilities and have been repaying their obligations since the insolvency petition date.
The £2.1 million claim that Eastwick had been including in the Halcyon Mutual Bank "set off amount" (i.e. the remaining demand charges for Commercial Lending's agreements until the end of the contract terms) was pulled out Eastwick's Motion.
The minimum account/pooling agreement monthly balance should no longer be required by the bank (Note: Originally Eastwick appeared to be using Commercial Lending's minimum balance to set off Treasury & Commercial Lending obligations). 

I would recommend that you challenge Eastwick's operations folks, if they continue to say that Commercial Lending must be keeping a minimum balance in your account. If you have any problems, please let me know and I will get our outside counsel involved again.

Thanks,
Julia Owen
</quoted>
